findings.title: Single point of failure
findings.description: Orders DB (SQL) runs as a single instance. 2 component(s) depend on it: Orders API, Inventory API.
findings.rationale: A component with one instance takes every dependent down with it during a crash, a deploy, or a host failure. Availability is capped by the weakest single instance.
findings.mitigation: Run at least two instances behind a load balancer or use a managed, zone-redundant tier. Make dependents tolerate a short outage with retries and a queue where writes can wait.
findings.fixHint: set-component-prop replicas >= 2 (and zones >= 2 for data stores)

findings.title: Credentials committed in source or configuration
findings.description: Orders API has credentials in its source or configuration files.
findings.rationale: Anything in the repository is visible to every developer, every CI runner, every fork and every leaked laptop. Secrets in config are the most common root cause of cloud account compromise.
findings.mitigation: Move secrets to a vault or the platform's secret store, inject them at runtime, rotate the exposed values now, and add a secret scanner to CI.
findings.fixHint: set-component-prop hardcodedSecrets = false; add-component secrets vault; add-flow service→vault

findings.title: Data store confined to one availability zone
findings.description: Orders DB (SQL) is not zone-redundant.
findings.rationale: Zone-level incidents (power, network, cooling) are the most common cloud outage class. A single-zone data store turns one of them into a full outage with possible data loss.
findings.mitigation: Enable zone-redundant storage or synchronous replicas across at least two zones.

findings.title: External dependency without a circuit breaker
findings.description: Orders API depends on external Payment Provider with no circuit breaker.
findings.rationale: Third-party outages are outside your control and often long. Without a circuit breaker every request keeps waiting on the dead dependency, exhausting the caller.
findings.mitigation: Wrap the call in a circuit breaker that opens after repeated failures and returns a fallback (cached value, degraded feature, queued retry).

findings.title: Data store without backups
findings.description: Orders DB (SQL) has no backup configured.
findings.rationale: Replication protects against hardware failure, not against bad deploys, ransomware, or a wrong DELETE. Without point-in-time backups those are unrecoverable.
findings.mitigation: Enable automated backups with point-in-time restore, test a restore, and keep a copy outside the primary account or region.

findings.title: Deep synchronous call chain
findings.description: 6 synchronous hops: Shopper (browser) → CDN → API Gateway → Storefront Web → Orders API → Inventory API → Orders DB (SQL).
findings.rationale: Each synchronous hop multiplies latency and failure probability. A chain of four or more services means the slowest or flakiest one dictates the user experience and any failure cascades to the top.
findings.mitigation: Break the chain with asynchronous messaging, cache intermediate results, or collapse services. Add timeouts and bulkheads at every hop.

findings.title: Unauthenticated call across a trust boundary
findings.description: API Gateway → Storefront Web crosses a trust boundary without authentication.
findings.rationale: Any caller that reaches the endpoint can impersonate a legitimate one. Trust boundaries exist precisely because the other side cannot be assumed friendly.
findings.mitigation: Require authentication on the receiving side: OAuth/JWT for user traffic, mTLS or managed identity for service-to-service traffic. Deny by default.

findings.title: Data in transit is not encrypted
findings.description: API Gateway → Storefront Web uses http.
findings.rationale: Cleartext traffic can be read and modified by anyone on the path: a compromised host, a misconfigured proxy, or a cloud-provider insider. Credentials and PII are the usual casualties.
findings.mitigation: Use TLS everywhere, including inside the private network. Prefer mTLS for service-to-service calls and enforce TLS on database and queue connections.
findings.fixHint: set-flow-prop encrypted = true; set-flow-prop protocol = https

findings.title: Public endpoint without rate limiting
findings.description: API Gateway is publicly reachable with no rate limiting.
findings.rationale: Without a request budget per client, one script can consume all capacity, run credential stuffing at full speed, or run up your cloud bill.
findings.mitigation: Enforce per-client rate limits and quotas at the gateway, with stricter limits on authentication and expensive endpoints.

findings.title: Synchronous call without a timeout
findings.description: Orders API calls Orders DB (SQL) synchronously with no timeout.
findings.rationale: A slow dependency holds threads and connections until the caller runs out. Without a timeout, a partial slowdown becomes a full outage that spreads upstream.
findings.mitigation: Set an explicit client timeout below the caller's own budget and fail fast. Pair it with a retry policy and a circuit breaker.

findings.title: Background work invoked synchronously
findings.description: Orders API → Notification Worker is a synchronous call into a worker; no queue in between.
findings.rationale: Calling a worker directly couples request latency to slow work and lets a traffic burst overwhelm it. A queue absorbs bursts and lets the worker fail without failing the request.
findings.mitigation: Put a queue or topic between the caller and the worker. Make the caller enqueue and return; make the worker idempotent.
findings.fixHint: add-component queue; add-flow caller→queue (isSync=false); add-flow queue→worker; remove-flow caller→worker

findings.title: No health check endpoint
findings.description: Orders API has no health check.
findings.rationale: Without a health probe the platform cannot detect a hung instance, restart it, or pull it out of the load balancer. Failures stay invisible until users report them.
findings.mitigation: Expose liveness and readiness endpoints that verify critical dependencies, and wire them to the orchestrator and load balancer.

findings.title: Database shared by multiple services
findings.description: Orders DB (SQL) is written by 2 services: Orders API, Inventory API.
findings.rationale: A shared database couples deployments, lets one noisy service starve the others, and makes schema changes a coordination problem. It is also a single blast radius.
findings.mitigation: Give each service its own schema or database, or at least separate connection pools and resource limits. Expose data via APIs or events instead of shared tables.

findings.title: Public-facing tier does not autoscale
findings.description: API Gateway is public-facing without autoscaling.
findings.rationale: Public traffic is spiky and adversarial. A fixed-size tier either wastes money or falls over under a campaign, a crawler, or a flash crowd.
findings.mitigation: Enable horizontal autoscaling on request rate or CPU with sensible min/max, and load test the scale-out path.

findings.title: Data at rest is not encrypted
findings.description: Orders DB (SQL) is not confirmed to be encrypted at rest.
findings.rationale: Disk snapshots, backups and decommissioned drives leave the security perimeter. Encryption at rest is the control that makes those leaks harmless.
findings.mitigation: Enable encryption at rest with customer-managed keys where regulation requires it, and include backups and snapshots.

findings.title: No audit trail on sensitive operations
findings.description: Orders DB (SQL) has no audit logging.
findings.rationale: Without an immutable record of who did what, you cannot investigate an incident, prove compliance, or dispute a fraudulent action.
findings.mitigation: Emit audit events for authentication, authorization decisions and data writes to a write-once store separate from application logs.

findings.title: Untrusted input not validated at the edge
findings.description: API Gateway receives input from Shopper (browser) without confirmed validation.
findings.rationale: Every injection class (SQL, command, template, deserialization) starts with input that was trusted too early. Validation at the boundary is the cheapest control you have.
findings.mitigation: Validate and canonicalize input against a schema at the first trusted component, reject on failure, and use parameterized queries downstream.

findings.title: No secrets manager in the architecture
findings.description: Services authenticate to Orders DB (SQL), Payment Provider, Email Service but no vault or managed identity is modeled.
findings.rationale: Services need credentials for databases and third parties. Without a vault or managed identities those credentials end up in config files, environment variables and CI logs.
findings.mitigation: Introduce a secrets manager or managed identities so no service holds long-lived credentials, and rotate automatically.
findings.fixHint: add-component secrets vault; set flows auth = managed-identity

findings.title: No secondary region for disaster recovery
findings.description: Orders DB (SQL) exists in a single region.
findings.rationale: Regional outages are rare but long. Without a replica or restorable copy in another region, recovery time is measured in days.
findings.mitigation: Geo-replicate the data store or ship backups to a second region and document the failover runbook.

findings.title: Synchronous call without retry policy
findings.description: CDN → API Gateway has no retry policy.
findings.rationale: Transient faults (connection resets, throttling, brief failovers) are normal in distributed systems. Without a bounded retry with backoff they surface as user-visible errors.
findings.mitigation: Add a bounded retry with exponential backoff and jitter for idempotent operations. Never retry without a timeout.

findings.title: No monitoring or logging component modeled
findings.description: The architecture has no monitoring, logging or alerting component.
findings.rationale: Mean time to recovery is dominated by mean time to notice. Without centralized logs, metrics and alerts, outages are discovered by customers.
findings.mitigation: Add centralized logging, metrics and tracing with alerting on error rate, latency and saturation for every service.

findings.title: Authentication mechanism not modeled
findings.description: Users are present but no identity provider is modeled.
findings.rationale: If nobody can point at where identities are issued and verified, authentication is probably ad hoc per service, which is where bypasses come from.
findings.mitigation: Model the identity provider explicitly and route all user and service authentication through it.
